media_strategy.selection_principle: Default to all five channels chosen in a data-driven way; the dataset is fundamentally about *audio* (an hour of recorded performance) so the audio channel here is an actual official Netflix-channel clip embed, not a sonification. Charts are minimal and architectural — three of them stripe the page and let the staircase, the depth-vs-laughter relationship, and the chapter map speak for themselves.

chart.reason: We have several quantitative comparisons (laugh-duration histogram, minute-by-minute profile, depth × laughter, chapter map, callback distance, climax staircase) that the prose claims rely on.

image.reason: Two atmospheric images frame the piece: an empty spotlit stage at the open and a stone archway at the close as a visual metaphor for structural support.

video.reason: image2video animates the teaser still (slow push-in, dust drift) so the opening feels like a curtain rising. Avoids generic event-reenactment video.

audio.reason: Two complementary audio decisions: (1) a real official Netflix-channel YouTube clip embedded inline in the climax section as an instance — readers can hear Wong's actual voice and feel the staircase rather than read about it; (2) a generated jazz-club ambience bed gated behind a click-to-play control on the page, evoking the Neptune Theater between bits without competing with the embedded clip.

interactive_or_map.reason: An interactive 'tree of topics' lets the reader explore the six-level nesting structure that the prose names as the architectural backbone. There's no map dimension to the data.

des_01.label: Teaser hero image — empty spotlit stage

content.prompt: Editorial photograph: a single empty stage spotlight beaming down from the rafters of an old theater, dust motes drifting through the cone of warm yellow light, the stage floor is a polished dark wood, deep shadows recede into black, no people, no text, atmospheric, cinematic, large format film aesthetic, mood of anticipation just before a comedian walks on

des_01.brief: A still image of a spotlit empty stage from above. No comic on stage yet — anticipation. The visual centrepiece of the teaser, used as the first frame of an image2video clip.
des_01.rationale: The dataset is a recorded live performance. A visual that evokes the room before the performance starts creates curiosity without revealing any finding.

des_02.label: Teaser motion — animated spotlight (image2video)

content.prompt: very slow parallax push-in toward the spotlight, gentle drift of dust particles falling through the cone of light, subtle flicker on the bulb, no camera shake, no people enter frame

des_02.brief: A 6-second loopable animation of the teaser image: very subtle parallax push-in, dust drifting through the spotlight beam. Plays autoplay-muted on page load.
des_02.rationale: We already have a strong still; image2video preserves the composition and adds the kinetic edge that pure stills lack — and audio comedy is fundamentally a kinetic, time-based art.

des_03.label: Stat callout — the unique 10-second laugh

content.label: the longest single laugh in the hour

des_03.brief: Big 80px stat showing '10s' with the label 'the longest single laugh in the hour' below. Sits at the very top of the first prose section, as the lede.
des_03.rationale: The peak is uniquely 10 seconds — exactly one caption out of 925. That singularity deserves a headline number, not a chart.

des_04.label: Laugh-duration histogram

style.palette: muted warm, single accent on the 10+ bar

des_04.brief: A bar chart of laugh-duration buckets across all 925 captions. The leftmost '0' bar dominates (573 captions); each successive bucket is smaller. The rightmost '10+' bar has count 1 — a tiny but visible accent-coloured bar that the reader can hover for the climax line. Annotation arrow on the '10+' bar saying 'one caption'.
des_04.rationale: The shape of the distribution — long tail with a single 10-second outlier — is the strongest visual proof of the 'rare detonations' point in the prose.

des_05.label: Stat callout — laughter share of the hour

content.label: of stage time is just the audience laughing — about 12 minutes of an hour

des_05.brief: Stat callout displaying 20.7% with caption explaining the framing.
des_05.rationale: 20.7% is a memorable, narratable number. It anchors the 'shape of the hour' section.

des_06.label: Minute-by-minute laughter chart

content.interaction: hover tooltip showing 'minute X — Ys of laughter'; vertical reference rule at minute 11 labelled 'climax line at 11:48'

style.palette: warm single-tone area fill (amber); no gridlines; minimal axis

des_06.brief: A 60-bin area chart of laughter seconds per minute of the special. Minute 11 has a clear local peak. Annotation marks the climax timestamp 11:48. Other peaks at minutes 8, 13, 33, 37 are visible but unlabelled.
des_06.rationale: An area chart treats laughter as a continuous wave through the hour — appropriate metaphor for a live audience reaction. Lets the reader see at a glance that the climax minute really is the loudest.

des_07.label: Topic tree explorer (interactive)

content.initial_state: A small bar chart shows the count of topics at each of the 6 levels (10, 21, 43, 31, 19, 7). Below it, a horizontal bar at the top represents level 1 (10 segments). Levels 2-6 are collapsed by default.
content.trigger: Click on a level to expand it, revealing the topics at that level as a row of small labelled segments.
content.transition: Smooth height transition; clicking again collapses.
content.payoff: Reader sees that the routine literally has 6 layers, with level 3 the broadest. Reinforces the prose claim that this set is a tree, not a list.

des_07.brief: A simple, restrained interactive: stack of horizontal bands, each band representing one level (1 at top, 6 at bottom), filled with small segments proportional to the topic counts. Click a band to reveal a tooltip with example topic names. No fancy node-link diagram — keep it readable.
des_07.rationale: The tree fact is the structural backbone of the argument. An interactive lets the reader engage with the depth claim without overwhelming a static chart.

des_08.label: Depth × laughter chart

content.interaction: hover tooltip showing avg, max, and caption count at each level

style.palette: two muted shades — one for avg, one for max; no gridlines

des_08.brief: Grouped bar chart with level on the x-axis (1 to 6) and two y series: average laugh seconds (primary, darker) and max laugh (secondary, lighter). Level 4 is the visible peak — it owns both the highest average curve approach and the lone 10-second max.
des_08.rationale: The data table has six rows and two metrics — a grouped bar makes the pattern pop in one glance: laughter rises with depth, max peaks at level 4.

des_09.label: The climax staircase chart

content.interaction: hover any bar to see its exact caption text in a tooltip

style.palette: monochrome warm; only the 11:48 bar in accent colour; the four big-laugh captions get small annotation labels
style.annotation: Each of the four laughs >= 4s gets a one-line label; the 10s bar's label is the climax line in italic quotes

des_09.brief: A horizontal-time bar chart showing 16 caption rows from 11:11 to 12:34. Each bar's height = laugh seconds. Reader sees the staircase: 1.0 → 1.0 → 3.0 → 1.5 → 0 → 4.0 → 0 → 10.0 → 0 → 6.0 → 6.5. The 10s bar at 11:48 is the visible peak. The label on it shows the exact climax line.
des_09.rationale: This is the load-bearing chart of the piece. The prose argues that the 10s laugh is the apex of a 24-second staircase; the chart must literally show that staircase.

des_10.label: The Netflix clip — Ali Wong on stage

content.caption: An official Netflix-channel clip from Baby Cobra. Wong on stage, seven months pregnant, in the room where the staircase was built.

des_10.brief: Standard YouTube iframe embed inside a styled card with rounded corners and a short caption below. Sits inside the climax section after the staircase chart, so the reader can hear how the bit actually sounds.
des_10.rationale: The dataset describes audio. Embedding the official clip turns the chart into something the reader can audibly verify. Strict rule: this embed_url is copied verbatim from detective.json inst_01 (verified: true).

des_11.label: Callbacks reach-back chart

content.interaction: hover to see the seed text and the callback text

style.palette: thin warm arcs over a neutral timeline; the 46-minute arc is the most prominent

des_11.brief: A horizontal timeline of the hour (0 to 60 min). Each of the three callbacks is drawn as an arc from its seed time to its callback time. The 46-minute arc (mom callback) is the longest and most prominent. Smaller text above each arc shows the callback label and reach-back duration.
des_11.rationale: Callback distance is fundamentally a 'reach' from one point in time to another. An arc visualisation literalises that reach across the hour-long horizontal axis.

des_12.label: Chapter map of the special

content.interaction: hover each segment to see span and laugh seconds; clicking pulses the corresponding row in a small table below

style.palette: five chapter colours, marriage clearly the biggest segment; intro and conclusion are tiny end-caps

des_12.brief: A single horizontal stacked bar representing the full hour, divided into the five level-1 chapters. The marriage segment dominates (30:40); pregnancy is second (19:20); paintball is a sliver (10s); intro/conclusion are end-caps. Below the bar is a small data table listing each chapter's span, laugh seconds, and laugh share — sortable by clicking column headers.
des_12.rationale: The chapter map answers a side question the prose raises: 'What do we mean when we say Baby Cobra is about pregnancy?' The hour is mostly about marriage.

des_13.label: Closing image — the architectural arch

content.prompt: Conceptual editorial photograph: a single tall stone archway under dramatic warm spotlight, the keystone at the top illuminated, the supporting voussoirs and pillars receding into shadow, a metaphor for architecture supporting a single peak moment, no people, no text, monochrome warm tones, large format film aesthetic, contemplative mood

des_13.brief: A still image of a stone arch with its illuminated keystone — visual rhyme for the argument that the climax line is the keystone of the structural arch. Sits alone at the bottom of the closing section.
des_13.rationale: The closing section explicitly invokes 'arch' and 'keystone'. A literal architectural still rhymes the prose without competing with it.

des_14.label: Generated club-ambience audio

content.why_audio: The chapter-map section transitions from analysis to closing reflection. A short bed of jazz-club ambience invites the reader to mentally relocate to the Neptune Theater for a moment. The clip is gated behind a click — not autoplay.
content.trigger: Click on a small 'Listen — the room' control just under the chapter map
content.ui_form: Small inline mini-player tucked into the chapter map's bottom right — no oversized waveform card.

content.prompt: A single sparse 30-second bed of warm jazz club ambience: muted standup bass walking line, soft brushed snare ticking quarter notes, very faint distant audience murmur and clinking glasses, no melody lead, low volume, instrumental, evokes a smoky comedy club between sets, no vocals

content.fallback: If audio is muted or unsupported, the chart and prose are complete on their own. The control is greyed and labelled 'audio unavailable'.
content.novelty_note: Avoids the generic 'click-to-play tone card' pattern by tucking the player inline beside the chapter map and only using it as atmosphere — not as a sonification.

des_14.brief: A small click-to-play control under the chapter map. When pressed, plays a 30-second jazz-club ambience clip. Visual fallback: the chart and prose are complete without it.
des_14.rationale: The dataset's other audio slot is the YouTube embed of the actual special. Adding a soft ambience bed elsewhere on the page complements rather than competes — and keeps audio earned by adding atmosphere the chart cannot supply.

page_rhythm.tone: warm dark editorial — the colour of stage lighting against black; serif body type; restrained accent colour reserved for highlighted data points
page_rhythm.text_visual_pattern: stat callout → prose → chart, repeated; one image at open and one at close; a single embedded video clip in the climax section
page_rhythm.anti_sameness_notes: Avoids the 'guess first quiz at the top' pattern. Avoids autoplay sonification cards. The teaser is a quiet still that becomes a slow video, not a flashy interactive. The page structure rhymes its argument: it builds, peaks at the climax-staircase chart, and comes back down through the chapter map and the closing image.
page_rhythm.typography_notes: Stat callouts at 64-80px, weight 700, with a thin label below. Body text Georgia / 18px / 1.6 line-height. Section titles in a system serif at 28px. Caption captions in italic at 14px. A single accent colour (warm amber, e.g. #d97a3a) used only on highlighted bars and the climax laugh.
